entry.title: The day we redrew the garden
entry.summary: After hearing the app looked rather dull overall, we reworked the garden screen from scratch.
entry.content:
We redrew the garden screen of Moss Garden, an idle game for iOS, after hearing that the design felt dull. It now has a deeper forest palette, a large garden scene with hills, a lotus pond and fireflies, and view-only decorations that never change the pace of the game.

Starting with color

The most honest feedback on the garden screen was that the design felt dull overall. So we started with color: a deeper forest background, with the moss and dew greens toned down so the screen stays easy on the eyes.

The garden scene

The top half of the screen is now a large garden scene: two layers of hills, a lotus pond, stars and a moon at night, fireflies at dusk, and a soft ripple when you water. A rounded panel below switches between plants and decorations.

Decorations

Decorations began with stepping stones, a fence, a bench and a stone lantern. They are for looking at only, so they have no effect on the pace of the game. Buying one places it in its spot right away, and moving it back and forth costs nothing.

Making things pretty never ends, so we stopped at one question: is this a screen you'd want to open every day?

FAQ

What changed on the Moss Garden garden screen?

The color palette, a large garden scene with hills, a lotus pond, stars, a moon and fireflies, and a panel that switches between plants and decorations.

Do decorations affect how the game plays?

No. Decorations are for looking at only, so they never change the pace of the idle game.

entry.title: Why show dew with decimals
entry.summary: The moss grows 0.1 per second, yet the dew counter looked frozen. This is how we fixed the number format.
entry.content:
Moss Garden is an idle (incremental) game for iOS, and its dew counter used to look frozen because it showed only whole numbers from ten upward. We now show two decimals below 1 and one decimal below 1,000, and we round down so the number never promises more than you have.

Why the number looked frozen

Moss was piling up at 0.1 per second, but the dew number at the top of the screen stayed the same for a long time. A tester told us they couldn't tell whether it was counting at all. The cause was simple: from ten upward we only showed whole numbers.

What we changed

Values below 1 now show two decimals, and values below 1,000 show one. Trailing zeros are dropped, so you read 289 instead of 289.0.

The one real decision was rounding. Showing 185.56 as 185.6 would make something you can't buy yet look affordable. So we round down instead: the number on screen is always at most what you actually have.

It is a tiny change, but in a game about waiting, watching the number move is part of the reward.

FAQ

Why does Moss Garden show dew with decimals?

Because the moss grows 0.1 per second, and whole numbers made the counter look frozen. Decimals let you see that it is counting.

Does the dew number round up or down?

Down. The number on screen is always at most the amount you actually have, so nothing looks affordable before it is.
